title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Creating Interlocking Ribbing
description: You can create exquisite interlocking rib effects in CLO in just 5 simple steps! CLO technical experts teach you practical tips! Start learning now!
transcript:
Hello everyone, I will show you how to make a colored pattern.  
First, find the pattern material in the window of the picture.  
Then apply it to the plate on the collar.  
Find the pattern of the pattern material in the attribute container.  
Use PS to open.  
Use PS to draw the color construction effect.  
The purple RGB value is the same as the dark purple in the close.  
Fill in its base color.  
Then build a new layer to fill in the white.  
You can use the marker tool to assist.  
Next, save it.  
This is the effect of the saved pattern.  
In close, replace the original pattern.  
You can use the edit pattern tool to adjust the position of the pattern.  
If you need to do a three-dimensional construction of the pattern,  
We need to make a corresponding call pattern in PS.  
Select a layer.  
Fill in the black.  
Copy the white layer.  
And merge the layers.  
Add this layer to blur the high-fiber.  
This is the high-fiber blur.  
This is the high-fiber blur.  
This is the high-fiber blur.  
This is the effect after the high-fiber blur.  
Save it.  
After saving, apply this call pattern.  
Adjust the call degree to 1.  
Adjust the particle diameter to 1.  
Turn on render.  
Let's see the effect.  
As you see, the value will be converted to 1 to 1.  
You can see the result here.  
Then, you do the same.

chunks.content: ## Creating Colored Patterns for Interlocking Ribbing in CLO and Photoshop This section explains the process of creating a colored pattern for interlocking ribbing using pattern materials, Photoshop (PS), and CLO software. Key terms include pattern material, RGB color values, layers, and pattern editing tools. 1. Locate the pattern material in the window of the picture. 2. Apply this pattern material to the plate on the collar in CLO. 3. Find the pattern material again in the attribute container. 4. Open the pattern material file using Photoshop (PS). 5. Use Photoshop to draw the color construction effect on the pattern. 6. Match the purple RGB value to the dark purple color present in CLO. 7. Fill in the base color accordingly. 8. Create a new layer and fill it with white to assist the pattern visibility. 9. Use the marker tool in Photoshop as needed to assist in filling. 10. Save the edited pattern file. 11. In CLO, replace the original pattern with the newly saved pattern. 12. Use CLO’s edit pattern tool to adjust the position of the pattern as needed. --- ## Creating Three-Dimensional Construction Patterns with High-Fiber Blur in Photoshop This section covers how to create a 3D effect for the pattern using Photoshop layers, merging, and a high-fiber blur technique. Terms include call pattern, layers, black fill, white layer copy, merging layers, and high-fiber blur. 1. Open the pattern in Photoshop and select the relevant layer. 2. Fill the selected layer with black. 3. Copy the white layer. 4. Merge the black-filled layer and the copied white layer. 5. Apply a high-fiber blur effect to the merged layer to create a soft, textured look. 6. Observe the effect of the high-fiber blur on the pattern. 7. Save the pattern after applying the blur effect. --- ## Applying and Adjusting Call Patterns in CLO This section describes how to apply the edited call pattern in CLO and adjust its rendering properties for the desired visual effect. 1. Apply the saved call pattern in CLO. 2. Set the call degree to 1. 3. Adjust the particle diameter to 1. 4. Enable rendering to view the effect. 5. The values convert to a 1:1 scale, and the result is visible in the render window. 6. Repeat the process as needed for other pattern areas. --- This process combines Photoshop editing techniques and CLO’s pattern application tools to create detailed, colored, and three-dimensional interlocking ribbing patterns optimized for garment design visualization.
